advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clear the bot backoff inline on bot deploy success (mirror mcp's clear_mcp_backoff at line 816) instead of relying only on the footer clear_backoff that early exits skip.
evidence: deploy_review_bot writes the marker but has no clear_backoff: `echo "$TARGET" > "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" "$BOT_SHA_FILE"` at autodeploy.sh:687, then `prune_docker_caches`/`log ... redeployed + healthy` and return
mcp mirror DOES clear inline: `clear_mcp_backoff` at autodeploy.sh:816 immediately after writing MCP_SHA_FILE

`clear_backoff` has exactly one call site (autodeploy.sh:886), inside the footer that is bypassed by `if [ "$bot_deferred" = 1 ] || [ "$bot_incomplete" = 1 ] || [ "$mcp_incomplete" = 1 ]; then exit 0` at autodeploy.sh:828
Concrete path: bot backoff window elapsed -> deploy_review_bot succeeds -> mcp delta pending with open window sets mcp_incomplete=1 -> exit 828 -> stale BACKOFF_FILE persists
advisory.finding: On bot success the shared bot backoff file is not cleared inline; it is cleared only at the footer (clear_backoff, line 886), which is skipped when the tick exits early at the incomplete/deferred guard (line 828) or on an mcp fatal exit. A bot that deployed successfully can therefore leave a stale deploy-backoff file (target==$TARGET, elapsed next-epoch, stale fail-count) — inconsistent with the mcp path, which deliberately clears its own backoff inline at line 816 to avoid depending on the footer.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `clear_backoff` inside deploy_review_bot right after writing BOT_SHA_FILE (near line 687), mirroring the mcp block's inline clear_mcp_backoff at line 816.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that seeds an unparseable/garbage value (e.g. 'zzzz') into mcp-deployed-sha (and bot-deployed-sha), with a git stub whose `rev-parse --verify` fails for that value, and assert the component still diffs from $DEPLOYED (deploys) rather than treating the garbage marker as a range endpoint.
evidence: Added script lines 548-551: `mcp_deployed="$(cat "$MCP_SHA_FILE" ...)"` then `if [ -z "$mcp_deployed" ] || ! git -C "$MIRROR_DIR" rev-parse --verify -q "$mcp_deployed^{commit}" ...; then mcp_deployed="$DEPLOYED"; fi`
Added script lines 552-555 apply the same guard for bot_deployed via BOT_SHA_FILE.

tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:1026 (the stub used by _mcp_box_shared_change): `rev-parse) cat "__TARGET_FILE__"; exit 0 ;;` — always succeeds, so a garbage marker such as writing 'zzzz' into mcp-deployed-sha would never drive the ! rev-parse fallback.
No new test writes an invalid/garbage sha into MCP_SHA_FILE or BOT_SHA_FILE and asserts the deploy still diffs from $DEPLOYED rather than treating the garbage marker as a valid range endpoint.
advisory.finding: The newly added marker-validation fallback (empty/unparseable component marker falls back to $DEPLOYED) is never exercised: the git stub used by every new test unconditionally returns exit 0 for `rev-parse`, so `git rev-parse --verify -q "$mcp_deployed^{commit}"` always succeeds and the fallback branch that guards against a poisoned diff range is dead in tests.
scenarios: A partially-written or corrupted mcp-deployed-sha marker on the box: the fallback should treat it as $DEPLOYED; if the guard regressed (e.g. dropped the rev-parse verify), the tests would stay green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the shared git stub so `rev-parse --verify -q <x>^{commit}` returns non-zero for a non-target sha, then add a test writing a garbage marker and asserting the mcp/bot block still computes the delta against $DEPLOYED.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 172 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 5774-fdb2-3d7f-4bab has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 5774-fdb2-3d7f-4bab` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 5774-fdb2-3d7f-4bab` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 5774-fdb2-3d7f-4bab --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
